title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 319: The Metaphorical Machine
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 319 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

The Metaphorical Machine: Embodied Cognition and Language

Paragraph 1. For many years, brain scientists thought the human mind worked just like a biological computer. Early computer experts believed thinking only meant moving symbols and rules inside the brain. In that old view, the human body was just simple outside equipment, and thinking happened completely separately from muscles or movement. Today, language experts Dr. Arthur Pence and Dr. Miriam Cho say this old computer idea is wrong.

Paragraph 2. Pence and Cho support a new theory called 'embodied cognition'. They argue that human thinking grows directly out of how our bodies move and feel in the real world. We use everyday metaphors—word pictures—to understand big ideas. For instance, we talk about time like walking: the future is 'in front of us', and the past is 'behind us'. We also describe kindness using temperature, like a 'warm' welcome or a 'cold' look.

Paragraph 3. Modern brain scans prove these word pictures are deeply connected to our bodies. When people read phrases like 'he grasped the idea', the brain lights up areas that control real hand movement and feeling rough surfaces. Our brain understands abstract thoughts by reusing the same body circuits we use to hold objects.

Paragraph 4. This discovery shows a major limit for artificial intelligence (AI). Computers have no living body and cannot feel real touch, warmth, or tiredness. Even though AI processes words at amazing speed, it has never felt a warm hug. Without a physical body that interacts with the real world, machines cannot truly understand human meaning.

groups.instructions:
Complete the notes below.
Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.

groups.title: Questions 5–8
groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

steps: Đoạn 4: "...cannot feel real touch, warmth, or tiredness."

q5.text: In the old scientific view, how did the human mind work?
options: B. Like a computer separate from the body

steps: Đoạn 1: Quan điểm cũ xem trí não như máy tính tách biệt khỏi cơ thể.

q6.text: Why do people use phrases like 'the future is in front of us'?
options: A. Because poets invented them for books
B. Because computers taught them to humans
C. Because we use body experiences to understand abstract ideas

steps: Đoạn 2: Ta dùng ẩn dụ gắn với trải nghiệm cơ thể (đi lại, nhiệt độ) để hiểu khái niệm trừu tượng.

q7.text: What do brain scans show when someone reads 'he grasped the idea'?
options: A. Brain areas used for holding objects light up.
B. The brain stops working for a few seconds.
C. Only the eyes are active while reading.

steps: Đoạn 3: Vùng não điều khiển cử động nắm tay sáng lên khi đọc ẩn dụ này.

q8.text: According to Paragraph 4, why can't AI truly understand human words?
options: A. It reads too slowly to finish long books.
B. It has no physical body to feel real-life experiences.
C. It does not have enough memory to store metaphors.

steps: Đoạn 4: AI không có cơ thể sống để cảm nhận cái ôm, hơi ấm hay sự mệt mỏi.
